narrative.northStar: The Quiet Instrument Over the Real Earth
narrative.overview:
The Earth is the interface. NASA GIBS imagery is the planet's surface (Blue Marble by day, city lights by night, true-colour swaths and cloud infrared as layers), the terminator is real, and the globe runs edge to edge. Everything else is a small set of exact instrument readouts pinned to the window's edges: a top bar, a layer rail, an event feed that the selected object's details replace, and a seven-day timeline. Chrome is opaque graphite-navy on a midnight ground, typed in Work Sans at light-to-medium weights with tabular figures, and it never competes with the planet.

Colour belongs to data. Markers carry four hue families plus glacier blue for orbital estimates; cyan exists only for the selected object and keyboard focus. The read pages (Events, Satellites, Sources, About) share the same ground, ink and type but slow down: a split hero with a light display headline on one half and a live working fragment of the product on the other, then a narrow reading column with generous section breaks and two-ended rows with nothing drawn between them.

The system refuses both the category default (a small boxed globe in a grid of KPI cards) and its opposite (a neon command-centre HUD with scan lines and glowing borders).
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed lit globe; chrome as opaque edge-pinned instruments, never frosted glass over WebGL.
Midnight ground, three-step graphite-navy surfaces, cool-white ink in three strengths.
Data colour in four families plus glacier for estimates; cyan reserved for selection and focus.
Work Sans 300/400/500, tabular figures on every number, sentence case throughout.
Hairlines inside panels only; depth from tone, with one shadow reserved for floating popovers.
The chrome POLARIS mark is the only metallic object.

rules.name: The Colour-Is-Evidence Rule
rules.body: Data colour uses four families only: heat amber, water/ice frost, quake coral rising to critical red at M6+, and sand for everything else. Glacier blue is reserved for satellite estimates. Category inside a family is told apart by its glyph, never by a new hue.

rules.name: The One Cyan Rule
rules.body: Cyan marks the selected object and keyboard focus. It is not a brand accent, not a button fill and not decoration.

rules.name: The Red-Means-Critical Rule
rules.body: Red appears only for M6+ earthquakes, unavailable feeds and errors.

rules.name: The Tabular Truth Rule
rules.body: Every count, time, coordinate, magnitude and age is set in tabular figures, usually paired with its unit or "UTC" in faint ink.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels, group heads and buttons are sentence case at normal tracking. Tracked capitals belong to the POLARIS wordmark alone.

rules.name: The Opaque Instrument Rule
rules.body: Panels over the globe are solid surface with a hairline border, never frosted, never glowing.

rules.name: The Shadow-Only-Floats Rule
rules.body: Only transient popovers and the hover tag cast shadows; docked panels and read pages are flat.

dos: **Do** let the globe own the viewport and pin chrome to the edges as opaque `surface` panels with a 1px `line` border.
**Do** colour data from the four families (amber, frost, coral to red at M6+, sand) and glacier for satellite estimates; distinguish categories within a family by glyph.
**Do** keep cyan for the selected object and keyboard focus.
**Do** set every number in tabular figures with its time, unit or source beside it in faint ink.
**Do** leave the open-space field as Cesium's real star skybox (about #040404) while panels and read pages sit on `ground`.
**Do** honour `prefers-reduced-motion`: entrances become a 160-200ms fade and press scaling stops.
**Do** give read-page heroes a live working fragment of the product, never a picture of it.
donts: **Don't** blur or frost panels over the WebGL globe.
**Don't** add a new hue for a new event category, or use red for anything but critical states.
**Don't** use cyan as a button fill, brand accent or decoration.
**Don't** add scan lines, glowing borders or HUD brackets; this is an instrument, not a command centre.
**Don't** box the globe into a card grid of KPI tiles.
**Don't** put chrome or metallic sheen anywhere except the POLARIS mark.
**Don't** add tracked uppercase labels or eyebrows above headings.
